images.title: Either base, its own height
images.purpose: Show that a parallelogram gives the same area with either side as base, each with its own perpendicular height.
images.composition: One parallelogram with two heights in two colours, one per base, and the two equal products underneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. A parallelogram with bottom side 10 units and slanting side 6 units, leaning right (corners at (0,0), (10,0), (13.6,4.8), (3.6,4.8)), very light grey fill. The bottom side drawn thick in #0072B2 labelled '10 cm'; the left slanting side drawn thick in #E69F00 labelled '6 cm'. A dashed #0072B2 height from the top left corner straight down to the bottom side (foot 3.6 units from the bottom left corner), right angle mark, labelled '4.8 cm'. A dashed #E69F00 height from the bottom right corner to the top left corner, perpendicular to the left slanting side, right angle mark at the top left corner, labelled '8 cm'. Below the figure two lines: '10 × 4.8 = 48 cm²' in #0072B2 and '6 × 8 = 48 cm²' in #E69F00.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Any side times its own perpendicular height gives the same area, 48 cm².
images.description: Show that a parallelogram gives the same area with either side as base, each with its own perpendicular height.
images.context: Concept T6.C2; one image showing only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: With these sides the angle has sine 0.8, so the perpendicular from the bottom right corner to the left side lands exactly on the top left corner; that segment has length 8.

image_decisions.why: Pairing each base with its own perpendicular height is a visual matching job; colour carries the pairing.
